purpose: Teach: 羽根/遊戯/製図/海面/浴室/祖父母/出稼ぎ/蔵書

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが羽根つきを孫と楽しまれた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he used to play badminton with the grandchildren.
lines.style: Soft, distant gaze into memory. Gentle opening, as if reaching back across decades. Quiet, almost speaking to himself. The voice of someone holding a small, warm moment from long ago.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、お部屋を遊戯室と仰ってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, and your father used to call that room the playroom, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm, affirming tone. She's meeting him in the memory, gently adding her own piece. Slight rise at the end—inviting him to continue, to keep remembering together. Tender without being sentimental.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは設計図の製図をされたぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he did drafting work—architectural plans.
lines.style: The same distant, gentle register. A pause before the detail, as if he's picturing it. Slow, deliberate. He's not just reporting facts; he's holding the image of his father bent over those plans.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、海面を眺めるのがお好きでらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And he loved watching the sea, didn't he, dear? I remember him doing that.
lines.style: Soft agreement, but with a slight catch—she's remembering something tender about him. The 'didn't he' is gentle confirmation, not a question. A small sigh underneath, the affection of long years together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと新しい浴室を作ったぞ
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he built a new bathhouse with me.
lines.style: A shift—quieter pride underneath the wistfulness now. Built. The word carries weight. His voice steadies slightly on that memory. Still distant, but more present in this one. The satisfaction of something made together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お孫様の祖父母として頼られたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He was so relied upon by the grandchildren as their grandfather, wasn't he?
lines.style: She's gentle but direct now. A statement more than a question. Her voice carries quiet pride in his role, in who he was to them. There's a tender understanding—she sees what he's saying without him having to say it all.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんは出稼ぎで都会に出られた
lines.en: Gran, when your father was young, he went to the city to work, to earn money for the family.
lines.style: A longer pause before this one. The wistfulness deepens—there's a thread of sacrifice in this memory. Quiet respect for that choice. His voice stays gentle but reaches back further, to a harder time.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、蔵書を毎日整えてらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He arranged his books every day, so carefully. He was a thoughtful man, your father.
lines.style: Close, intimate tone now. She's sitting beside him in this memory. Slight break in the voice—the awareness that these small habits are what remain. The voice wavers just slightly with affection and the weight of time passing.
